data.q: Which attribute marks a test method in xUnit?
data.e: xUnit uses [Fact] for simple test methods. [Test] is NUnit/MSTest, [TestMethod] is MSTest, [TestCase] is NUnit parameterized tests.

data.q: Which attribute marks a parameterized test method in xUnit?
data.e: xUnit uses [Theory] combined with [InlineData], [MemberData], or [ClassData] for parameterized tests. [TestCase] and [DataRow] are NUnit/MSTest.

data.q: In NUnit, which attribute is used to specify test case data for a parameterized test?
data.e: NUnit uses [TestCase] to provide inline arguments for a test method. [InlineData] is xUnit, [DataRow] is MSTest.

data.q: What is the xUnit equivalent of NUnit's [SetUp] attribute?
data.e: xUnit uses the test class constructor for per-test initialization (equivalent to NUnit's [SetUp]). It does not have a [SetUp] attribute.

data.q: What is the xUnit equivalent of NUnit's [TearDown] attribute?
data.e: xUnit uses IDisposable on the test class for cleanup (equivalent to NUnit's [TearDown]). The Dispose method runs after each test.

data.q: Which assertion method is used in xUnit to check equality?
data.e: xUnit uses Assert.Equal(expected, actual). Assert.AreEqual is MSTest/NUnit classic, Assert.That is NUnit constraint model.

data.q: In NUnit's constraint model, which syntax is used to assert that a value equals 5?
data.e: NUnit's constraint model uses Assert.That(actual, constraint). Is.EqualTo(5) is the constraint.

data.q: How do you assert that an exception is thrown in xUnit?
data.e: xUnit uses Assert.Throws<T>(delegate) which returns the caught exception for further inspection.

data.q: How do you assert that an exception is thrown in NUnit (constraint model)?
data.e: NUnit constraint model uses Assert.That(delegate, Throws.TypeOf<T>()) or Throws.InstanceOf<T>().

data.q: Which attribute in NUnit marks a method to run once before all tests in a fixture?
data.e: NUnit uses [OneTimeSetUp] (formerly [TestFixtureSetUp]) for fixture-level setup. [SetUp] runs before each test.

data.q: Which attribute in xUnit marks a method to run once before all tests in a test class?
o: xUnit does not support this directly; use IClassFixture or collection fixtures
data.e: xUnit intentionally omits [BeforeAll]/[AfterAll] attributes. Shared setup uses class constructors (per test) or IClassFixture/ICollectionFixture for shared context.

data.q: What is the purpose of the [Trait] attribute in xUnit?
o: To mark a test as ignored
data.e: [Trait("Category", "Integration")] adds metadata to tests, enabling filtering in test runners (e.g., dotnet test --filter Category=Integration).

data.q: In NUnit, which attribute is used to ignore a test temporarily?
data.e: NUnit uses [Ignore("reason")] to skip a test. [Explicit] requires explicit selection to run. xUnit uses [Fact(Skip = "...")].

data.q: Which xUnit attribute allows sharing a fixture instance across multiple test classes?
data.e: ICollectionFixture<T> shares a single fixture instance across all test classes in a collection. [Collection] defines the collection; IClassFixture shares per class.

data.q: What is the main difference between xUnit's [Fact] and [Theory]?
o: [Fact] runs once; [Theory] runs multiple times with data
[Fact] is for synchronous tests; [Theory] is for async
data.e: [Fact] denotes a single test case. [Theory] denotes a parameterized test that executes once per data set (via [InlineData], etc.).

data.q: Which test runner command runs only tests with a specific trait in xUnit?
data.e: xUnit traits are filtered via `dotnet test --filter "Trait=Category=Unit"`. The filter syntax uses the trait name and value.
